correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, arcs are threshold comparisons of independent send/receive uniforms. Reciprocal-pair moments follow from a symmetric two-sample kernel and the exact shared-endpoint covariance 7/144. The sink–reciprocity covariance integrates distinct and incident pairs; sink–source covariance integrates their unique shared comparison. The four marginal endpoint point processes converge jointly to independent Poisson processes, and the self-comparison omission has probability <=1/(n+1) per count. The Hoeffding first projection is U_i(1-W_i), with degenerate residual variance O(n^2); a joint Laplace–Fourier expansion makes its Gaussian limit independent of the four endpoint processes. All proof steps are in RESULT.md. A checker independently enumerates all 2n! rank orders for n=2,3,4 and tests 1221 exact assertions. No finite experiment is treated as proof of an infinite claim.

value.rationale: The canonical threshold-digraph model already has its one-sided zero-degree and global arc statistics studied. Reciprocal pairs quantify bidirectional relationships rather than total arc density, so their dependence on source/sink obstructions is a natural missing observable. Three explicit exact covariance signs quantify finite network dependence, while the full independent geometric–geometric–Gaussian limit identifies how boundary-degree effects decouple from bulk reciprocity. This gives a substantively motivated joint network-statistic law, not a minor reparameterization of the known marginal source/sink results.
